fact: THE UNTRIED RECORD CLASS, AND A COUNTY-BY-COUNTY SURVIVAL SURVEY. ARGUMENT: Aaron (10) and Joseph (7) are in NO Caton household in Fauquier, Fairfax or Prince William in 1830 (C082, C166, C167) while small daughters remain at home (C082), and both brothers ended in the SAME TRADE - Aaron a tailor in 1850, Joseph a tailor by his own biography and the 1883 county history (C076, C191). Two brothers gone from home at 7 and 10 and both trained to one trade is the signature of a BOUND APPRENTICESHIP. This class has never been searched on the Virginia side: in 191 claims 'overseer' appears once (C154) and unrelated; C141/C142 searched OHIO indentures. WHAT EXISTS: (1) FAUQUIER COUNTY (VA.) BOARD OF OVERSEERS OF THE POOR MINUTES, 1804-1845 - ONE VOLUME, Local Government Records Collection, Fauquier County Court Records, Library of Virginia; barcode 1125621, FAUQUIER COUNTY REEL 116, filmed by Backstage Library Works under LVA's Circuit Court Records Preservation Program. The minutes give 'the names of people receiving financial support, food, and clothing, as well as BINDING CHILDREN AS APPRENTICES, and the burial of the deceased.' Covers 1828-1836 exactly. (2) Virginia Auditor of Public Accounts, OVERSEER OF THE POOR ANNUAL REPORTS AND CHECKLISTS (APA 739) - independent state-level series, Fauquier holdings 1829-1851. (3) Fauquier County MINUTE BOOKS survive from 1759 (microfilm and index books, Virginiana Room, Warrenton Library); Fauquier is NOT a lost-records county. WHAT THE RECORD YIELDS: under County Court supervision the Overseers indentured children to masters to learn a trade; the entry gives the names of the overseers, the child, the master, the date, and the trade to be taught. Virginia bound out orphans AND 'children whose parents could not support them or who failed to educate or instruct them' - SO A LIVING FATHER IS NORMALLY NAMED. TWO CAUTIONS. (a) PRINCE WILLIAM IS DEAD GROUND: its Overseers of the Poor minutes survive only 1788-1802 (Dettingen Parish, published Historic Dumfries 1976) and the county is an LVA Lost Records Locality. FAUQUIER IS THE ONLY CANDIDATE COUNTY WHERE THIS RECORD SURVIVES FOR 1828-36 - and the county where the family demonstrably was in 1823-35 - so the test is cheap and bounded. (b) DO NOT USE LVA's 'Virginia Untold: Indentures of Apprenticeship, 1777-1893': it is free and indexed and it is the WRONG INDEX - Virginia Untold is LVA's African American narrative project and that series covers indentures of free Black and mixed-race children. White apprenticeships stay in the OP minutes and county order books, unindexed. (c) No published abstract covers the target years - the Sparacio/Heritage Books Fauquier Minute Book Abstracts stop in the 1780s; reel 116 must be read directly. PREMISE TO TEST FIRST: OP binding presupposes a destitute or dead father, so the theory needs Thomas poor. That is readable from pages ALREADY LOCATED AND NEVER OPENED - C156's 17 Full-Text hits, including 'Caton Thomas 2' in the 1809-19 volume and both 'Thomas' and 'Thomas Jr' in the 1820-32 volume. The property columns say whether he was poor; the same run dates when 'Thomas Jr' becomes a separate tithable, which independently tests C193. ALSO: a father could bind a son PRIVATELY by indenture recorded in the Deed or Minute Books - search both.
